answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks via progressive quartz bonding: each identity locks a compute proof whose difficulty spirals higher proportional to the detected size of any shared-operator cluster, while a public sable reputation marker (non-transferable, epoch-decaying only via independent graded work) bars low-score clusters from mining or grading payouts. Attackers incur rising hardware time and capital lockup per fake identity plus permanent reputation isolation that nullifies earnings, making large farms cost more in coordination and resources than they can recover.
